topic: The Geometry of the Windmill: Solving the IMO 2011 Problem
target_audience: High school students interested in competitive mathematics and geometry

outline.topic: The Geometry of the Windmill: Solving the IMO 2011 Problem
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in competitive mathematics and geometry

sections.title: The Hook: Meet Milly the Laser Robot
sections.content: Introduce the premise of the problem using a character-driven scenario. Explain the setup: a set of points (stars) on a flat plane and a rotating line (a laser beam).
sections.example: Milly the Robot stands in a field of glowing stars. She holds a long laser beam that rotates clockwise. The goal is to see how the beam 'jumps' between stars.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Pivots and Rotation
sections.content: Review basic geometry concepts: what a pivot point is, the nature of 180-degree rotation, and how a line divides a plane into two half-planes.
sections.example: Visualizing a see-saw: one point is the fixed center (pivot). If we rotate the see-saw 180 degrees, the 'left' side becomes the 'right' side.

sections.title: The Core Rule: The Hand-off
sections.content: Define the 'Windmill' movement rule. A line rotates around a pivot point until it hits another point in the set. At that exact moment, the hit point becomes the new pivot, and the rotation continues.
sections.example: An animation of a rotating baton. As soon as the tip of the baton touches a bystander, that person grabs the center and the baton starts spinning around their hand instead.

sections.title: The Invariant Property: The Balancing Act
sections.content: Introduce the 'Aha!' moment: the 'Number of Points on One Side' property. Explain that as the line rotates and changes pivots, the number of points on the left side of the line remains constant.
sections.example: Imagine 5 sheep in a field. If the laser line starts with 2 sheep on its left, no matter how many times it 'hits' a new sheep and changes pivots, there will always be exactly 2 sheep on the left side.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Visualization (3-Point Case)
sections.content: Walk through a full 180-degree rotation cycle using a simple triangle of points to show how the pivot moves and how the line returns to its original orientation.
sections.example: Point A is the pivot. The line hits Point B (Pivot B). It then hits Point C (Pivot C). After 180 degrees, the line is parallel to its start position, but the 'left' and 'right' sides have swapped.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Infinite Loop
sections.content: Summarize the conclusion: because the number of points on each side is invariant and there are a finite number of points, the process must eventually repeat. This proves the windmill will hit every point if started correctly.
sections.example: A final top-down view showing the 'Windmill' tracing a beautiful, symmetrical flower-like pattern as it infinitely cycles through the stars.

storyboard.title: The Hook: Meet Milly the Laser Robot
lecture_lines: Meet Milly, a robot in a field of stars.
She holds a laser beam that rotates clockwise.
Today, we explore how this beam moves.
animations: Create a field of several small white circles (#FFFFFF) representing stars scattered randomly on a black background.
Introduce a long cyan line (#00FFFF) passing through one star, rotating slowly clockwise.
The laser beam hits a second star, and the center of rotation instantly shifts to that star.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Pivots and Rotation
lecture_lines: A pivot point is the center of rotation.
Rotating a line 180 degrees swaps its sides.
This divides the plane into two distinct halves.
animations: Focus on one yellow star (#FFFF00) as the center of a rotating white line (#FFFFFF).
Color the regions on either side of the rotating line in light magenta (#FF00FF, opacity 0.2) and light green (#00FF00, opacity 0.2).
Rotate the line 180 degrees and show the magenta and green regions swapping positions as the line flips.

storyboard.title: The Core Rule: The Hand-off
lecture_lines: The laser rotates around its current pivot point.
It continues until it hits another star.
Instantly, that new star becomes the pivot.
The rotation continues from this new center.
This "hand-off" creates the windmill motion.
animations: Show a cyan line (#00FFFF) rotating clockwise around a yellow pivot star A (#FFFF00).
The line rotates until it makes contact with a white star B (#FFFFFF).
Star B flashes and turns yellow (#FFFF00) while Star A turns white (#FFFFFF), indicating the pivot has changed.
The cyan line continues rotating clockwise, now using Star B as its center of rotation.
Repeat the sequence: the line hits a third star C, which then becomes the new yellow pivot star.

storyboard.title: The Invariant Property: The Balancing Act
lecture_lines: Watch the stars on one side of the line.
As the line rotates, stars stay on their side.
During a hand-off, the count remains the same.
This invariant property is the key to the proof.
No matter the pivot, the balance never changes.
animations: Highlight all stars currently to the left of the rotating laser in orange (#FFA500).
As the laser rotates towards star B, show that star B is the next point the beam will encounter.
The line sweeps through star B; stars already on the left remain on the left.
After the pivot shift to star B, show that the set of orange stars on the left has not changed.
Display a counter 'Stars on Left: n' at the top, which stays constant during the pivot hand-off.

storyboard.title: Step-by-Step Visualization (3-Point Case)
lecture_lines: Start with the laser pivoting at Point A.
It rotates and hits Point B, its new pivot.
Next, it hits Point C and continues spinning.
After 180 degrees, the line returns to Point A.
Notice how the sides have now completely swapped.
animations: Draw three stars A, B, and C in a triangular formation on the plane.
The laser starts at star A, rotates clockwise, and 'hands off' the pivot to star B.
The laser rotates from star B, hits star C, and then rotates from star C back to star A.
Show the laser line returning to its original horizontal orientation after a total rotation of 180 degrees.
Draw a faint grey dotted path (#555555) connecting A, B, and C to show the pivot's movement.

storyboard.title: Conclusion: The Infinite Loop
lecture_lines: The invariant side-count ensures a repeating cycle.
With finite stars, the windmill hits every point.
Geometry transforms a simple rule into an infinite dance.
animations: Accelerate the animation, showing the laser quickly cycling through various stars in the set.
As the laser hits each star, it briefly glows to show it has been part of the windmill process.
Fade out the points and line to leave behind a complex, symmetric pattern of the line's history.
